name: KVL_GAMMA_LIP
comment: Biochemical split of the feed organic matter from its elemental composition: Kleerebezem, R. and van Loosdrecht, M.C.M. (2006). Waste characterization for implementation in ADM1. Water Sci. Technol. 54(4):167-174, doi:10.2166/wst.2006.538 (decision log C1e). Per C-mol of organic matter CH_y O_z N_v (N at the oxidation state of NH3), the degree of reduction is gamma_SUB = 4 + y - 2z - 3v - u (their eq. 7; u = charge from neutralized VFA, taken as 0 for solid feeds). Protein, carbohydrate and VFA have gamma = 4, the model lipid (glycerol tripalmitate, C51H98O6, C1H2.85O0.575 per C-mol; their Table 1 and footnote 1) has gamma_LIP = 5.68, so a substrate more reduced than 4 contains lipids: eta_LIP = (y - 2z - 3v - u) / (gamma_LIP - 4)          (their eq. 9) eta_PR  = v / N_PR,  N_PR = 0.26 N-mol per C-mol      (Table 1, Fig. 2) eta_CHO = 1 - eta_LIP - eta_PR - eta_VFA                (Fig. 2) (C-mol fractions). COD shares follow from COD_i ~ eta_i x gamma_i / 4 (their eq. 10), normalized to the total. Used here with the measured elemental analysis (C, H, O, N of the sampled composition) instead of their COD/TOC route: checked by hand at the F15 central compositions, the elemental route gives lipid COD shares of 0.30 (food waste), 0.066 (dairy manure), 0.33 (sewage sludge), against 0.40, 0.047 and 0.14-0.26 measured by Fisgativa et al. 2020; the COD/TOC route on Fisgativa's own Table 2 gives 0.48 for manure and 0.72 for secondary sludge. The authors warn that the split is very sensitive to the measured oxidation state (their Fig. 4); hence the bounds (recorded as caps). Assumption: the degradable part (fD) has the same biochemical split as the whole organic matter (fD and the split come from different sources). S is ignored, as in the source. e-mol per C-mol, model lipid (Table 1)
